note: Both sets cover the same core facts from the notes and wiring schedule, with identical quotes and largely identical claims. The only substantive difference is the NFDS enclosure claim: Set A correctly names the device simply "NFDS" as the page does, while Set B invents the qualifier "DC NFDS" for a device the page never describes as DC. Set A is therefore slightly more faithful, with no invented content.
remarks: Both sets repeat several facts under two names (MAIN BREAKER rating 150 A vs 150A/2P; NFDS rating 200A/2P vs 200 A; MAIN PANEL phase '1 phase' vs '1'; GND connection conductor vs wire size; Wiring 150 #4G ground wire vs ground conductor size; Wiring 34 #10G ground conductor vs ground wire). Both also omit schedule rows 50 (AL: 3#6, #8G., 1"C.), 33 (CU: 6#10, 3#10G., 1"C.) and 10 (CU: #12/2WG.), plus the MAIN BONDING JUMPER note and the voltage/current sensor connections. Minor: several claims put the conduit size (e.g. 3/4"C.) in the conditions field rather than as a conduit attribute.
